newsitem.title: USA: Ore. report calls for rejection of Enron, PGE deal.
newsitem.headline: Ore. report calls for rejection of Enron, PGE deal.

text.p: The Oregon Public Utility Commission on Friday recommended rejection of the proposed $2.1 billion merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Corp, the parent of Portland General Electric Co (PGE).
A staff report said "Enron has not shown that the merger would serve Portland General Electric customers in the public interest, as required by state law."
The staff warned previously it would not recommend the merger without a guaranteed rate reduction of $141 million for Oregon electricity customers.
But Enron has officially offered a rate cut of just $61 million.

In a statement today, the staff said it believes the fundamental difference between the proposed rate cuts is that Enron's offer fails to include sufficient customer compensation for losses or potential risks from the merger.
A spokesman for Enron said the company has not yet had a chance to review the full report, but is "still optimistic that the merger will be approved."
Comments on the staff's proposed order are due April 29, and the commission will hear oral arguments at a public meeting on May 6.
June 4 is the date the three-member commission is scheduled to make a final ruling on the merger.
